sections.title: The letter té
paragraphs: The letter is named (té) /te/. Its main sound is a consonant, as in (table) /tabl/, which means a piece of furniture with legs. A consonant is a sound made when the mouth blocks or narrows the air. This letter has three different sounds across French words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, press the tip of your tongue against the upper front teeth. Stop the air for a moment, then release it cleanly without voice. Touch your throat to feel that it does not shake. For the next sound, bring your teeth close together. Blow air smoothly over the tongue tip to create a clear hiss.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: At the start of words or before most vowels, it sounds as in (tapis) /ta.pi/. You also hear this sound inside words, such as in (porte) /pɔʁt/. Before the letter i followed by another vowel, it sounds like an s in (patient) /pa.sjɑ̃/ or (démocratie) /de.mɔ.kʁa.si/. At the end of many words, it is a silent letter, as in (salut) /sa.ly/ and (petit) /pə.ti/.

sections.title: Tips for English speakers
paragraphs: Do not puff air when you say this letter, as you do in top. Place your tongue right against the back of your teeth, not on the ridge above them. Keep the sound dry and short. At the end of a word, remember not to pronounce the letter at all.
